questions.subject: science
questions.question: Due to the effect of which force are the celestial bodies in the universe situated at their position?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force pulls celestial bodies toward each other. It helps keep them in their positions and orbits.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which theory is considered the most realistic theory about the origin of the universe?
questions.explanation: Big Bang Theory explains the origin of the universe. So it is considered the most realistic theory here.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: According to the Big Bang theory, how did the universe originate?
options: From the collision of celestial bodies
From the explosion of a star
From the explosion of an atom
questions.explanation: Big Bang Theory says the universe began from a huge explosion. The option says explosion of an atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: According to Hubble’s theory, which fact is correct?
options: There is no relation between speed and distance of galaxies
The farther away the galaxies are, the lesser speed they will have
The farther away the galaxies are, the more speed they will have
The gravitational force of the galaxies does not affect their speeds
questions.explanation: Hubble's law says farther galaxies move faster. So speed increases with distance.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Under what condition can an open universe be hypothesized?
options: Average density is greater than critical density
Average density and critical density are not comparable
Average density and critical density are equal
Average density is less than critical density
questions.explanation: An open universe has average density less than critical density. Then the universe keeps expanding.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the meaning of H in Hubble’s law, v = Hd?
questions.explanation: In v = Hd, H means Hubble's constant. It is the constant of proportionality.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the universe?
options: The vast area around us containing celestial bodies
questions.explanation: The universe is the vast space around us. It contains stars, planets, galaxies and other celestial bodies.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following is a celestial body mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: A comet is a celestial body. It is found in space like planets and stars.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is formed by a group of many stars?
questions.explanation: A galaxy is a very large group of stars. So many stars together form a galaxy.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In which galaxy is the Solar System located?
questions.explanation: Our Solar System is in the Milky Way galaxy. So Milky Way is the correct galaxy.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which branch studies facts about the universe including its history and future?
questions.explanation: Universe science studies the universe. It studies its facts, history and future.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does astrophysics study according to the chapter?
options: Origin, structure and future of the universe
questions.explanation: Astrophysics studies the origin, structure and future of the universe. It is related to space science.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What force exists mutually among all celestial bodies in space?
questions.explanation: All celestial bodies have mass. So they attract each other by gravitational force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does the Moon revolve around the Earth?
options: Because of gravitational attraction between Earth and Moon
questions.explanation: Earth's gravity pulls the Moon. So the Moon revolves around Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do planets revolve around the Sun?
options: There is no force on planets
questions.explanation: The Sun's gravity pulls the planets. This gravity keeps planets moving in their orbits.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What did Hubble discover about galaxies?
options: Every galaxy is moving away from other galaxies
questions.explanation: Hubble found that galaxies are moving away from each other. This supports the expanding universe idea.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does v represent in Hubble’s law?
questions.explanation: In Hubble's law, v means velocity. It is the speed of galaxies moving away.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does d represent in Hubble’s law?
questions.explanation: In Hubble's law, d means distance. It shows distance between galaxies.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the value of Hubble’s constant mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Hubble's constant is 73 km/s/Mpc. It is used in v = Hd.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What model activity is used to show the expansion of the universe?
questions.explanation: When a balloon with dots expands, the dots move farther apart. It shows how galaxies move apart as the universe expands.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does Hubble’s study support the Big Bang theory?
options: It shows no relation with distance
It proves galaxies are fixed forever
It shows galaxies moving away, meaning they were closer in the past
questions.explanation: Galaxies are moving away now. So they must have been closer in the past.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to the size of the universe according to the Big Bang explanation in the chapter?
options: It is fixed from the beginning
It is increasing slowly but continuously
It becomes smaller every second only
questions.explanation: The universe is still expanding. Its size is increasing slowly and continuously.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to the speed of celestial bodies due to gravitational force during expansion?
options: It becomes zero at the beginning
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls celestial bodies toward each other. So it decreases their separating speed.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is critical density?
options: Average density required to stop the expanding universe
Density of a single star only
Density of a liquid in a beaker
questions.explanation: Critical density means density needed to stop expansion. It decides the future of the universe.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens in an open universe?
options: The universe continues to expand forever
All bodies become one atom at once
questions.explanation: In an open universe, bodies keep moving away. So the universe continues to expand forever.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens in a flat universe?
options: The universe becomes a chemical salt
Expansion gradually stops and the universe remains stable
questions.explanation: In a flat universe, expansion slowly stops. Then the universe becomes stable.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens in a closed universe?
options: Celestial bodies come closer and the universe may collapse
questions.explanation: In a closed universe, gravity pulls bodies back. So the universe may shrink and collapse.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is Big Crunch?
options: Collapse of the vast universe into a single point
questions.explanation: Big Crunch means the universe collapses into a point. It is the opposite idea of expansion.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which factor mainly determines the future of the universe according to the chapter?
options: Gravity depending on mass and size or density
questions.explanation: Average density controls the strength of gravity. So it helps decide the future of the universe.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If average density equals critical density, which universe is described?
questions.explanation: If average density equals critical density, the universe is flat. Less gives open, and greater gives closed.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If average density is greater than critical density, what future is suggested?
questions.explanation: Greater density means stronger gravity. It can stop expansion and pull the universe back.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement compares open and closed universes correctly?
options: Both must stop exactly at the same time
Open expands forever, while closed may shrink back
questions.explanation: An open universe expands forever. A closed universe may shrink back.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do celestial bodies not collide while moving in their orbits?
options: There is no gravity between them
Their motion and gravitational force maintain orbital paths
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls celestial bodies, and motion keeps them moving. Together they maintain orbits.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is meant by saying the universe was in a compressed state before the Big Bang?
options: Mass and energy were concentrated in a very small energetic state
All stars were already separated far away
There was no force at all
questions.explanation: Before the Big Bang, mass and energy were packed in a very small state. That state was highly energetic.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which four forces are said to have unified before the explosion?
options: Magnetic, digital, chemical and audio forces
Gravitational, electromagnetic, strong nuclear and weak nuclear forces
Solar, lunar, atomic and weather forces
questions.explanation: These are the four fundamental forces. They are gravitational, electromagnetic, strong nuclear and weak nuclear forces.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does the balloon-dot activity help explain Hubble’s conclusion?
options: Dots move farther apart as the balloon expands, like galaxies separating
questions.explanation: As the balloon expands, the dots move farther apart. This is like galaxies moving away in the universe.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which evidence in the chapter suggests the universe was once at one point?
options: Galaxies are moving away from each other now
questions.explanation: Galaxies are moving away from each other now. This suggests they were once closer together.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A galaxy is 2 Mpc away in Hubble’s relation with H = 73 km/s/Mpc. What separation speed is obtained?
questions.explanation: Use v = Hd. So v = 73 x 2 = 146 km/s.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which quantity does the net gravitational force in the universe depend on through mass and volume?
questions.explanation: Average density means mass in a given volume. It helps control the net gravity of the universe.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which sequence best represents a closed-universe life cycle idea from the chapter?
options: Big Bang, expansion, Big Crunch, possible new universe
Flat universe, no movement, no gravity, no mass
Only Hubble law, no origin, no future
questions.explanation: In a closed universe, expansion may stop and reverse. Then Big Crunch may happen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which conclusion follows from the statement that galaxies farther away move faster?
options: Earth is the only moving body
questions.explanation: Farther galaxies move away faster. This shows the universe is expanding.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to gravitational force when the distance between celestial bodies increases?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force decreases when distance increases. Far bodies attract each other less strongly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: According to Newton’s gravitation note in the chapter, gravitational force is directly proportional to what?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force increases with the product of masses. Larger masses give stronger attraction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: According to Newton’s gravitation note, gravitational force is inversely proportional to what?
options: Square of the distance between centres
questions.explanation: Gravitational force decreases with square of distance. So more distance gives much less force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which condition makes celestial bodies continue moving away forever?
options: Velocity becomes zero while gravity remains
Gravity becomes zero while some velocity remains
Velocity and gravity become zero together
Average density becomes greater than critical density
questions.explanation: If gravity becomes zero while speed remains, bodies keep moving away. So the universe expands forever.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which condition gives a stable flat universe?
options: Gravity and velocity become zero at the same time
Velocity remains but gravity becomes zero
Gravity remains after velocity becomes zero
Density is less than critical density
questions.explanation: A flat universe becomes stable when gravity and velocity end together. So both become zero at the same time.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which condition leads to Big Crunch?
options: Gravitational effect remains after velocity becomes zero
Gravity becomes zero first with velocity remaining
Average density is less than critical density
questions.explanation: If gravity remains after velocity becomes zero, it pulls bodies back. This can lead to Big Crunch.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does the Milky Way example show about the size of the universe?
options: The Solar System is outside all galaxies
There are no stars in galaxies
The universe is extremely vast with huge galaxies
questions.explanation: The Milky Way has many stars and huge distances. This shows the universe is extremely vast.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is the Big Bang theory considered reliable in the chapter?
options: It is based on chemical reaction rates
It denies the movement of galaxies
It explains galaxies moving away from each other
questions.explanation: Galaxies moving away support Big Bang Theory. It means the universe was once closer together.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which comparison is correct for flat and closed universes?
options: Flat universe becomes stable; closed universe may shrink and collapse
Closed universe has density less than critical density
questions.explanation: A flat universe becomes stable. A closed universe may shrink and collapse.
